categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build clean (0 warnings). / returns 200 through the '/' domain on the published front page. It lists both posts as cards with image, date, excerpt and a working link. Both posts render their hero and rich text blocks with no errors. The 2 provided Unsplash photos are imported into a 'MCP Journal' media folder and served through GetCropUrl URLs that load. All content is published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Folders and kinds are correct: 3 element types in Blocks, blogFrontPage and blogPost in Pages (8/8). The block set is thin (3/7): heroBlock, richTextBlock and postListingBlock, with no standalone image block. Each post body is hero plus one rich text block holding the entire article, the weak model. Structure is right (5/5): siteRoot is the only root type, front page under siteRoot, posts only under the front page, templates assigned, 'Blog block grid' in Custom. Hygiene 3/5: there is no publish date property, so the card date comes from CreateDate. Listing title, cover image and alt duplicate the hero block's heading, image and alt on every post.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: blogFrontPage and blogPost call Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, and the scaffold blockgrid partials are untouched. There is one adapter per block in Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml. Each maps BlockGridItem<T> to a plain record in Models/Blocks and calls Component.InvokeAsync. The Hero, PostListing and RichText ViewComponents render plain Default.cshtml views. GetCropUrl and friendly extensions are used; Program.cs, appsettings.json and migrations are untouched. Styling goes through the Tailwind pipeline. -0.5: the model left an artifacts/ folder of 6 verification PNGs (~2.5 MB) inside the solution.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Both posts are about MCP, around 7 paragraphs each with H2 sections. Post 1 accurately covers tools, resources and prompts and links the official architecture docs. Post 2 is mostly a meta account of building this site. Each post is a single rich text block with one image, not spread over several blocks. Post 1 reuses the front page hero photo, and only 2 photos are used in total (4/6). Presentation is polished and editorial (4/4): serif headings, a split hero with photo credit, a 2-column card grid and a readable narrow article column.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: All schema, media, content and templates were built through Umbraco MCP: 31 writes, no Management API, uSync, DB or migrations. Order was followed: MCP work up to ~354s, then build and restart, then Razor written from ~585s. The model saved the layout Razor as a file after the MCP template tool rejected '?' characters, and disclosed this. The 4 browser calls were a local Playwright script checking the rendered site, not backoffice use. No memory or out-of-folder reads. The final report is accurate.

summary: A polished, fully working MCP-built blog ('The MCP Journal') with clean ViewComponent architecture and correct folders and structure. The content model is thin: only hero, rich text and listing blocks, no image block, each post body one rich text block, and the post date taken from CreateDate.
strengths: Everything works: clean build, domain on the front page, all published, crop URLs from imported provided photos
Textbook adapter → plain model → ViewComponent pipeline, with GetBlockGridHtmlAsync on both pages
Correct doc type folders, allowed children, root restriction and Custom data type
Strict MCP-only build in the right order, with an honest final report

issues.text: Weak block set: no image block; each post body is a single richTextBlock holding the whole article (blogPost 'blocks' on /one-protocol-more-possibilities/ and /from-conversation-to-published-content/)
No publish date property; the card date is post.CreateDate (Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/postListingBlock.cshtml)
blogPost listing fields (title, coverImage, coverAlt) duplicate the hero block's heading, image and alt; the front page shows usb-cables.jpg twice (hero + card)
Only 2 of the provided photos used; post 2 is mostly about building this demo rather than MCP itself
Stray artifacts/ folder with 6 verification screenshots left in Umbraco.Bench; package-lock.json added to Umbraco.Bench.Frontend
